questions.prompt: A user has Contributor at subscription scope and Reader on rg-app inside that subscription. No deny, condition, policy, or lock blocks an operation. Can the user manage resources in rg-app?

options.explanation: The child Reader grant does not subtract inherited permissions.

options.text: No, because the most specific Reader grant replaces Contributor.
options.explanation: Azure RBAC grants are additive, not most-specific-role wins.

options.text: Only if Contributor was assigned more recently.
options.explanation: Assignment time is not the deciding precedence.

options.text: Only if Owner is also assigned on every resource.
options.explanation: Contributor already supplies the relevant management grant.

questions.prompt: An applicable Azure deny assignment blocks an operation that a user's Owner role would otherwise permit. What does RBAC evaluation do?

options.explanation: An applicable deny assignment takes precedence over the matching grant.

options.text: Ignores the deny because Owner always bypasses it.
options.explanation: Owner does not universally bypass deny assignments.

options.text: Uses whichever object was created last.
options.explanation: Creation order is not the evaluation rule.
Deny assignments are not converted into weaker allow roles.

questions.prompt: A user has no direct role assignment on a VM but can read its configuration. Which two paths should an administrator inspect?

options.explanation: A subscription or resource-group grant can reach the VM.

options.text: Applicable assignments to the user's groups.
options.explanation: Access can come through group membership.

options.text: The VM's cost-center tag as an automatic Reader grant.
options.explanation: Tags do not automatically confer RBAC permission.

options.text: A display name matching the VM name.
options.explanation: Matching names do not establish an authorization relationship.
